title: TMA and mbarrier: transpose with asynchronous copies

steps.title: Single tile: TMA load → mbarrier → transpose → TMA store
Persistent multistage ring buffer: full/empty barriers
128B swizzle and 4×4 register transpose: removing bank conflicts

cases.name: tiny
cases.purpose: Smaller than one box: the TMA zero-fills the out-of-bounds part and clips it on write-back. Values equal the linear input index, so an error shows where the data was read from.

cases.name: tail
cases.purpose: 4 more than a multiple of 32 in both directions: the coordinates of the tail boxes and the expect_tx byte count (the out-of-bounds part counts too).

cases.name: row
cases.purpose: Only 4 rows: 4 columns after the transpose, which tells transpose and copy apart; most of the y box is out of bounds.

cases.name: tall
cases.purpose: Tall, thin matrix: the conversion from tile index to (row, column).

cases.name: ring
cases.purpose: Each persistent CTA processes about 7 tiles: the ring buffer wraps around, and a wrong phase/parity or empty barrier reads a stale tile. The coordinate pattern pinpoints the error.

cases.name: ring_tail
cases.purpose: The ring buffer wraps around while both directions have tails: the lap and stage of a tail box are not fixed, so the byte count of the out-of-bounds zero fill and the parity must both be correct.

cases.name: big
cases.purpose: 256 MB of input, far larger than the 126 MB L2: measures HBM bandwidth utilization, directly comparable with lab 00.

cases.name: wide
cases.purpose: Non-square, also 256 MB: the rows of y (4096 floats) are shorter than the rows of x.
